mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact corporate earnings and thus drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, this hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which may lead to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns in the short term.
failure_condition: If UNRATE drops as specified but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate increases while unemployment is low, it may signal tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting equity markets over two months.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by >0.25% in 1 month and UNRATE < 4%
failure_condition: If the specified conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 30% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, higher federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, negatively affecting corporate profitability and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, the hypothesis is invalid.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests higher economic activity, which can lead to improved corporate performance and positive S&P 500 returns over the next two months.
failure_condition: If INDPRO growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of cases, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in housing starts indicates increased demand in the housing market, which may boost related sectors and lead to positive S&P 500 returns in the next month.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases as specified but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 45% of cases, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth slows while federal funds rates are high, it may indicate economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over two months.
failure_condition: If the conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 25% of cases, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong payroll growth in a low unemployment environment may lead to wage inflation, potentially causing the Fed to tighten policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns in the short term.
regime_hint: low unemployment with strong job growth
failure_condition: If payroll growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 50% of cases, the hypothesis is invalid.
